title: INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme 2026: Applications Open for Law Enforcement Officers and Criminal Investigation Experts Worldwide
summary: The International Criminal Police Organization, better known as INTERPOL, has opened applications for its Enhanced Secondment Programme , a major international professional opportunity designed to strengthen global law enforcement cooperation by bringing qualified police officers, law enforcement specialists and government officials from INTERPOL Member Countries into its international operational environment. The programme provides an opportunity for experienced law enforcement professionals to contribute their expertise to international efforts against transnational crime while gaining exposure to complex international policing operations, investigative techniques, advanced technologies and multinational cooperation. The opportunity is based within INTERPOL s operational structures, with the vacancy announcement indicating multiple duty stations and a secondment duration of 36 months . The programme is associated with Grade 5 positions and requires candidates to meet INTERPOL s eligibility, professional experience, endorsement and security requirements. According to the vacancy notice, the programme is intended to create a dynamic and secure pool of vetted law enforcement specialists who can be deployed or assigned according to operational needs, ensuring that the right expertise is available to address international crime challenges. About the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme INTERPOL is the world s largest international police organization, with 196 member states . Established in 1923, the organization facilitates cross-border police cooperation and supports authorities and organizations whose missions involve preventing and combating international crime. Through the Enhanced Secondment Programme, INTERPOL is seeking qualified law enforcement officers and experts who can strengthen its global operational capabilities and help the organization provide high-quality services to Member Countries. The programme is particularly relevant to professionals whose careers involve criminal investigations, intelligence analysis, cybercrime, financial crime, border security, organized crime, environmental crime, counter-terrorism, forensics, operational coordination, training, information management and other specialized law enforcement functions. The vacancy notice identifies the position as the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Program , reporting to coordinators within operational directorates. Although the vacancy page identifies Lyon, France as the location of the published opportunity, the detailed vacancy information specifies multiple duty stations , reflecting the international and operational nature of the programme. Key Details of the Opportunity Opportunity: INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme Organization: INTERPOL Vacancy Notice: 1663 Publication starting date: August 2, 2026 Location indicated on the vacancy page: Lyon, France Duty stations: Multiple duty stations Duration: 36 months Grade: Grade 5 Security clearance: Basic/Enhanced Application deadline: Applications are received throughout the year Eligible applicants: Qualified law enforcement and governmental officials from INTERPOL Member Countries Application route: INTERPOL Recruitment Hub through the organization s vacancies page Endorsement: Applications must be officially endorsed and submitted through the relevant National Central Bureau (NCB). What Is the Objective of the INTERPOL Secondment Programme? The programme aims to establish a pool of vetted law enforcement specialists capable of supporting INTERPOL s international operational requirements. The objective is to maintain a dynamic, secure and interoperable global repository of specialists who can provide the right expertise at the right time in response to international crime and policing challenges. This approach enables INTERPOL to strengthen cooperation between Member Countries and improve its ability to coordinate responses to transnational criminal activity. For participating officers, the programme can also provide exposure to an international working environment where professionals from different national law enforcement systems work together on shared security and criminal justice challenges. Who Can Apply? The Enhanced Secondment Programme is specifically targeted at professionals already working within law enforcement and government structures in INTERPOL Member Countries. Eligible categories identified in the vacancy include: Active police officers Serving police officers can apply where their professional experience and specialization correspond to the operational areas sought by INTERPOL. Law enforcement officers from national agencies This includes professionals working in agencies such as customs, border control and anti-corruption units, as well as other national law enforcement bodies. Civil servants working in law enforcement or government administrations Government officials whose responsibilities are directly connected to law enforcement or relevant national government functions may also be considered. The vacancy specifically states that the announcement applies to law enforcement and/or governmental officials within INTERPOL Member Countries. Areas of Expertise Sought The Enhanced Secondment Programme covers a broad range of criminal justice, policing and operational specialties. Prospective candidates may be considered for different Grade 5 operational positions depending on their professional background and expertise. Examples include: Criminal Intelligence Officer Professionals in this area may contribute to the analysis and dissemination of intelligence concerning transnational crime and support international efforts to identify and respond to criminal threats. Specialized Officer Specialized officers may work on particular crime types or specialist operational areas, including fugitives, disaster victim identification, cybercrime, human trafficking and financial crime. Regional Specialized Officer These professionals support regional operations by bringing localized knowledge and expertise relevant to particular geographical or operational environments. Criminal Intelligence Analyst Criminal intelligence analysts may collect, analyze and interpret criminal-related data and activities while supporting crime prevention and investigative operations. Crime Areas Covered by the Programme INTERPOL has identified a broad, non-exhaustive list of crime areas and policing capabilities that candidates can select as areas of interest within their applications. 1. Financial Crimes Relevant areas include: Anti-corruption Money laundering and asset recovery Fraud and financial crimes Counterfeit currency and security documents These areas are increasingly important in international law enforcement because financial investigations can reveal criminal networks operating across multiple jurisdictions. 2. Cyber and Digital Forensics The programme also covers emerging digital crime areas such as: Cybercrime Darknet investigations Cryptocurrency tracing Ransomware analysis Artificial intelligence fraud detection Professionals with specialized digital investigation and cyber-forensics experience can therefore find their expertise relevant to the programme. 3. Transnational and Organized Crime This broad category includes: Human trafficking and smuggling networks Online crimes against children War crimes and illicit arms Vehicle crime Drug trafficking Works of art Illicit goods and global health Intellectual property crime and digital piracy Public health and pharmaceutical crime These areas reflect the international nature of modern organized crime and the need for law enforcement agencies to collaborate across borders. 4. Environmental Crime Applicants with expertise in environmental enforcement may have experience in: Wildlife crime Fisheries crime Forestry crime Pollution Illegal mining Environmental crime can involve sophisticated cross-border networks, making international cooperation particularly important. 5. Counter-Terrorism and Extremism Relevant expertise includes: Counter-terrorism Chemical and explosives terrorism prevention Radiological and nuclear terrorism prevention Bioterrorism prevention Candidates working in these specialized security areas may therefore find the programme aligned with their professional expertise. 6. Forensics and Bio-Crime The vacancy identifies several forensic and identification-related areas, including: DNA analysis Biometrics Disaster victim identification Fingerprints and facial recognition Border control Counterfeit currency and security documents These capabilities can play an important role in international criminal investigations and identification processes. 7. Capacity Building and Training Professionals with experience in training and institutional development may be considered in areas such as: Training and development Digital curriculum design and operations This reflects INTERPOL s emphasis not only on operational investigations but also on strengthening the capabilities of law enforcement institutions. 8. Command and Coordination The programme also includes expertise in: Operations coordination, planning and support Communication assistance and information management Critical regional operations languages Professionals in these areas can contribute to coordination between different operational teams and Member Countries. 9. Global Outreach and Regional Assistance Candidates with experience in international or regional coordination may contribute to: Coordination of regional activities Support to National Central Bureaus This area is particularly relevant to professionals experienced in working with multiple institutions and stakeholders across jurisdictions. 10. Criminal Intelligence Analysis and Fusion The programme also seeks expertise in: Collection, analysis and interpretation of criminal-related data and activities Open-source intelligence and analysis These skills are increasingly important as law enforcement agencies deal with large amounts of structured and unstructured information originating from multiple sources. Main Duties and Responsibilities Successful seconded officers will be expected to contribute to INTERPOL s operational objectives under the supervision and guidance of management. The responsibilities are designed around addressing specific crime phenomena and supporting coordination of criminal cases and business continuity within existing activities. Key duties include: Coordinating investigations and cases between Member Countries. Identifying, establishing and maintaining professional contact with experts in relevant fields. Organizing and participating in training programmes. Participating in expert group meetings and conferences. Monitoring and analyzing information relating to the assigned area of activity. Developing remedies and best-practice solutions to challenges affecting the effectiveness of law enforcement agencies. Identifying major criminal threats with potential global impact. Developing strategic partnerships with national, sub-regional, regional and global organizations. Serving as a point of contact for Member Countries seeking assistance or advice in the relevant area. Carrying out other responsibilities assigned by the supervisor or organizational hierarchy. The programme therefore requires candidates who can combine technical or investigative expertise with communication, coordination, analysis and international cooperation skills. Education and Academic Requirements Candidates are expected to have three to four years of university-level study or other specialized higher education . The vacancy indicates that academic backgrounds in the following areas are particularly relevant: Law Public policy Police management Related disciplines Equivalent legal or police academy qualifications may also be considered. Importantly, the vacancy provides an alternative pathway for candidates who do not possess the required educational qualifications. Such candidates must demonstrate 10 years of relevant professional experience . Professional Experience Requirements Applicants should have substantial practical experience relevant to law enforcement and criminal investigations. The vacancy requires: At least three years of hands-on experience in police operations or criminal investigations. Specialization in one or more areas of transnational crime. Extensive experience as a law enforcement officer. A strong background in specialized criminal investigations. Regional, sub-regional and/or national operational police support experience. International experience is highly desirable, particularly experience gained through employment with an international organization, participation in international working groups or involvement in joint international projects. Applicants should therefore carefully match their professional experience with the crime areas and operational functions identified by INTERPOL. Language Requirements Professional fluency in English is required , including both written and oral communication. Knowledge of additional languages is considered an asset. The vacancy specifically identifies: French Spanish Arabic Other languages as useful additional language capabilities. Given the international environment in which INTERPOL operates, strong communication skills can be particularly important for professionals who will coordinate with colleagues, experts and authorities from different countries. Additional Skills Required In addition to academic and professional qualifications, applicants should demonstrate relevant technical and professional skills. The vacancy identifies: Sound investigative skills Strong written communication skills Strong oral communication skills Public speaking ability Presentation and briefing skills Computer literacy Familiarity with presentation software Knowledge of business intelligence software Knowledge of word-processing software These skills complement the technical law enforcement experience required for the programme. National Central Bureau Endorsement Is Essential One of the most important aspects of the application process is the requirement for official endorsement through the applicant s National Central Bureau (NCB) . Candidates are required to: Complete their application online through the INTERPOL Recruitment Hub. Submit the completed application together with a Support Letter or Letter of Nomination from their respective NCB. Candidates working in non-police law enforcement agencies should coordinate with their designated NCB before submitting their application. Ensure that the application is endorsed and submitted through the NCB. The vacancy clearly states that only applications endorsed and submitted through the NCB will be considered. Applicants should therefore not treat the NCB endorsement as an optional administrative step. It is a central component of the application process. Secondment Financial and Administrative Arrangements Prospective applicants should also understand that the secondment arrangement places several financial and administrative responsibilities on the officer s home administration, agency, service or government. According to the vacancy notice, the home administration or government is responsible for the officer s: Salary or remuneration Social insurance Pension contributions Welfare benefits Family allowances Benefits during the assignment Travel expenses Removal expenses associated with arrival and departure Other related costs depending on the circumstances Candidates are required to obtain written confirmation from their home administration, agency, service or government that it agrees to the applicable Conditions of Secondment. This confirmation should then be forwarded to INTERPOL through the relevant NCB. Applicants should therefore consult the applicable Conditions of Secondment and engage their relevant national authorities before proceeding too far with the application. Professional Development and Career Growth The programme can provide participating officers with valuable exposure to international law enforcement cooperation and professional development. The vacancy identifies several professional development opportunities associated with secondment, including: Greater awareness of complex international working environments. Development of cultural bridges and cross-border professional relationships. Advancement of policing, investigative and operational coordination skills. Exposure to cutting-edge technologies. Opportunities to pursue an international career. Opportunities for professional growth. Membership in a global network of law enforcement experts. INTERPOL also indicates that career progression may be possible through its learning and training activities. Successful experience in an Officer role, combined with relevant leadership development, could potentially lead to mid-executive positions such as: Coordinator or Operations Coordinator at Grade 4. Senior Coordinator or Senior Operations Coordinator at Grade 3. Diversity and Inclusion INTERPOL states that it aims to maintain a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcomes applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. The organization particularly welcomes applications from women and nationals of underrepresented or unrepresented Member Countries . However, recruitment remains merit-based, meaning that hiring decisions are based on candidates qualifications and the operational needs of the organization. Application Deadline There is no fixed closing date stated for this opportunity . The vacancy specifies: Deadline: Applications received throughout the year. However, applicants should not interpret this as a reason to delay preparation. Because the programme involves NCB endorsement, government approval and supporting documentation, eligible professionals should begin the process early enough to obtain the necessary institutional support. How to Apply Applications should be submitted online through the Vacancies section of INTERPOL s recruitment platform. The vacancy specifically directs candidates to use the recruitment page and emphasizes that applications must be endorsed and submitted through the appropriate National Central Bureau. Before applying, candidates should: Review the Conditions of Secondment applicable to the programme. Confirm their eligibility based on their law enforcement or government status. Identify the crime area or specialist field that best matches their professional experience. Prepare a detailed and accurate application highlighting relevant operational experience. Contact and coordinate with the relevant National Central Bureau. Obtain the required Support Letter or Letter of Nomination. Secure written confirmation from the home administration regarding the Conditions of Secondment and associated responsibilities. Complete the online application through the INTERPOL recruitment system. Ensure the application is formally endorsed and submitted through the NCB. The official INTERPOL website provides access to the organization s recruitment and career information. APPLY HERE What Applicants Should Emphasize in Their Applications Because the programme is highly specialized, applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates how their professional background corresponds with INTERPOL s operational needs. Strong applications should clearly explain relevant experience in areas such as: Criminal investigations Transnational crime Criminal intelligence Cybercrime and digital investigations Financial investigations Counter-terrorism Human trafficking Drug trafficking Border control Forensics Wildlife and environmental crime Intelligence analysis International police cooperation Operations coordination Training and capacity building Information management Open-source intelligence Candidates should avoid submitting generic descriptions of their professional duties. Instead, they should demonstrate their actual responsibilities, specialized expertise, operational exposure and experience working with other agencies or jurisdictions. Where applicable, applicants should also highlight experience in international working groups, cross-border investigations, joint operations, international conferences, regional initiatives and collaborative projects. Why the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme Is Significant The programme comes at a time when criminal networks increasingly operate across national borders and exploit technology, financial systems, transportation networks and digital platforms. Effective responses therefore require law enforcement agencies to share intelligence, coordinate investigations and develop common approaches to emerging threats. The Enhanced Secondment Programme provides a mechanism through which experienced national law enforcement professionals can contribute their expertise within an international policing environment while strengthening their own professional knowledge and networks. The programme s broad coverage of financial crime, cybercrime, organized crime, environmental crime, terrorism, forensics, intelligence, training and operational coordination also demonstrates the wide range of expertise required to address modern transnational crime. Visit HERE for more information about the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme 2026. Conclusion The INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme 2026 presents a significant international professional opportunity for qualified police officers, law enforcement specialists and relevant government officials from INTERPOL Member Countries. With a stated 36-month duration , Grade 5 classification and multiple operational areas, the programme is designed to strengthen INTERPOL s global operational capacity while giving participating professionals the opportunity to work within an international law enforcement environment. The opportunity is particularly relevant to professionals with strong backgrounds in criminal investigations, police operations, intelligence, cybercrime, financial crime, organized crime, counter-terrorism, forensics, environmental crime, border control, training, information management and operational coordination. Applicants should pay particular attention to the NCB endorsement requirement , the Conditions of Secondment and the financial responsibilities of their home administration. They should also ensure that their academic qualifications, professional experience, language abilities and specialist expertise are clearly aligned with the requirements outlined in the vacancy. Since applications are accepted throughout the year , there is no single fixed application deadline. Nevertheless, eligible professionals are encouraged to begin the process early, particularly because obtaining institutional endorsement and the required documentation may take time. For qualified law enforcement and governmental professionals seeking international exposure, specialized professional development and the opportunity to contribute to global efforts against transnational crime, the INTERPOL Enhanced Secondment Programme offers a potentially valuable pathway into international law enforcement cooperation. title: British Council International Consultant for Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) in Sudan 2026: Application Guide, Requirements and Deadline
summary: The British Council is seeking an International Consultant or Consultancy Firm for the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) initiative in Sudan , offering an important opportunity for experienced education, skills-development and policy professionals to contribute to the development of a comprehensive national framework designed to recognise skills acquired through formal, non-formal and informal pathways. The consultancy will provide technical support for the development of a National Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework in Sudan , with particular attention to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), Non-Formal Education (NFE), higher education, qualifications, assessment, certification, institutional governance and quality assurance. Applications for the consultancy close on 26 August 2026 . The successful consultant or consultancy firm will be expected to provide technical leadership and work with national stakeholders and development partners to develop a comprehensive, cross-sectoral National RPL Policy Framework that is operational, implementable and ready for government endorsement. About the British Council International RPL Consultancy in Sudan The British Council is implementing this initiative through its Youth Skills Programme in Sudan , which is supporting system-level reforms within Technical and Vocational Education and Training and Non-Formal Education. The broader objective is to improve young people s access to employment and lifelong learning opportunities. The need for a Recognition of Prior Learning system is particularly significant within the Sudanese context. Ongoing conflict and displacement mean that a considerable amount of skills acquisition takes place through informal and non-formal channels. People may develop valuable competencies through work, community activities, informal training, apprenticeships and other experiences without necessarily receiving formal qualifications recognising what they have learned. When such competencies remain unrecognised by formal education and training systems, individuals can face difficulties progressing into further education or securing employment that appropriately reflects their capabilities. The British Council initiative therefore seeks to help address the gap between skills acquired outside conventional formal education and the qualifications and recognition available through established systems. Background to the Recognition of Prior Learning Initiative The consultancy does not begin from scratch. It builds on earlier policy work and stakeholder engagement concerning Recognition of Prior Learning in Sudan. In March 2026 , the British Council convened a national Policy Dialogue on Recognition of Prior Learning. The dialogue brought together stakeholders including: Ministry of Education; Ministry of Higher Education; Ministry of Labour; Supreme Council for Vocational Training and Apprenticeship; National Centre for Curriculum and Educational Research; Private-sector representatives; Trade unions; Civil society organisations; and Development partners. The national dialogue produced two particularly important outputs. The first was a Policy Brief outlining key principles and system components required for Recognition of Prior Learning. The second was a Roadmap identifying phased steps for designing and implementing an RPL system. The Policy Brief identified critical areas such as regulatory frameworks, institutional arrangements, financing, quality assurance and stakeholder engagement. Meanwhile, the Roadmap established a phased pathway covering system design, implementation and continuous improvement. The new consultancy is intended to build upon these foundations and move the process towards a comprehensive National RPL Policy Framework that can ultimately be considered for government endorsement. Why the National RPL Framework Is Important for Sudan Sudan s political, economic and humanitarian circumstances have placed considerable pressure on the country s skills system and labour market. Conflict has disrupted education, contributed to widespread displacement and severely constrained or rendered non-operational parts of the education system. At the same time, young people represent a substantial proportion of Sudan s population, while unemployment remains high and the informal economy plays a dominant role. These circumstances create significant challenges for young people attempting to enter skilled, sustainable employment. Sectors with potential for economic growth require workers equipped with practical competencies and professional skills. However, disruption to education and limited access to quality learning have increased the importance of developing a skills system that is responsive, inclusive and resilient. A well-designed Recognition of Prior Learning framework could help create mechanisms through which existing competencies can be assessed, recognised and potentially connected with qualifications, further learning and employment pathways. Programmes Supporting the Initiative The activity forms part of the British Council s Going Global Partnerships (GGP) and Youth Connect programmes in Sudan. Going Global Partnerships supports mutually beneficial higher education and TVET collaboration between the United Kingdom and other countries. The programme aims to contribute to stronger, more inclusive and globally connected tertiary systems capable of supporting economic and social growth. Youth Connect, meanwhile, supports young people in developing the skills, confidence, inspiration and connections required to address major challenges including employability, inequality, conflict and climate change. The RPL consultancy therefore sits within a broader effort to strengthen education, skills development and opportunities for young people. Purpose of the British Council RPL Consultancy The British Council intends to appoint an individual consultant or consultancy firm capable of providing technical guidance and support to Sudan s TVET and Non-Formal Education systems. A central responsibility will be the development of a National Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework aligned with Sudan s TVET, NFE and higher education systems. The assignment is expected to ensure that the resulting framework supports both horizontal and vertical mobility between non-formal, technical and academic pathways. This is important because an effective RPL system should not merely acknowledge previously acquired competencies. It should also help establish pathways through which recognised learning can support progression between different parts of the education, training and qualifications system. The consultant or firm must consequently work towards an operational and implementable framework covering areas such as: Governance; Assessment; Certification; Quality assurance; Institutional responsibilities; Policy and legal provisions; Qualifications; Mobility between learning pathways; and Practical implementation. The consultant will also facilitate a co-creation process involving national stakeholders and development partners to strengthen national ownership and prepare the framework for endorsement. Scope of Work for the International RPL Consultant The consultancy involves an extensive scope of work covering policy design, institutional governance, assessment, certification, quality assurance, implementation, stakeholder consultation and endorsement support. 1. System Design and Policy Development The consultant or consultancy firm will begin by reviewing and consolidating the existing RPL Policy Brief and Roadmap. The assignment will require analysis of Sudan s existing: Legal landscape; Institutional environment; and Qualifications landscape. Using this analysis and the existing policy work, the consultant will design a comprehensive National Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework. The framework is expected to address: Policy provisions; Legal provisions; Integration with national qualifications frameworks; and Cross-sectoral articulation involving TVET, Non-Formal Education and higher education. This component is fundamental because the RPL system must be connected to Sudan s broader education, training and qualifications architecture rather than operating as an isolated mechanism. 2. Institutional Architecture and Governance A national RPL system requires clearly defined institutional responsibilities. The consultant will therefore define the roles and responsibilities of relevant institutions and stakeholder groups, including: Ministry of Education; Ministry of Higher Education; Ministry of Labour; Supreme Council for Vocational Training and Apprenticeship; National Centre for Curriculum and Educational Research; Training providers; Employers; and Civil society organisations. The consultant will also propose an appropriate national governance model. This is expected to cover matters including: Coordination mechanisms; Oversight structures; Implementation responsibilities; and Institutional arrangements required for effective administration of the RPL system. Recommendations may also involve establishing new RPL units or mechanisms or strengthening existing institutional structures where appropriate. 3. Competency-Based Assessment and Certification Model Another major component of the consultancy concerns the way people s existing competencies will actually be assessed and formally recognised. The consultant will develop a competency-based RPL assessment framework . Potential assessment methodologies specifically identified within the assignment include: Portfolios; Practical tests; and Interviews. The framework must also address certification pathways and equivalency mechanisms. Additionally, the consultant will consider credit transfer and articulation systems , helping establish how recognised competencies could contribute towards qualifications or progression between different education and training pathways. 4. National RPL Quality Assurance Framework Recognition will only have meaningful long-term value if institutions, employers, learners and other stakeholders can have confidence in the quality and consistency of the system. The consultant will therefore design a national quality assurance system for RPL. This will include: National standards; Guidelines; Accreditation mechanisms; Monitoring arrangements; Evaluation processes; and Continuous improvement mechanisms. The quality assurance framework will be important in supporting consistency, credibility and sustainability across the wider RPL system. 5. RPL Implementation Guidelines and Operational Manual The assignment extends beyond high-level policy development. The British Council requires a framework capable of being implemented in practice. The consultant will therefore develop a detailed Operational Manual . The manual is expected to provide guidance concerning: Step-by-step implementation processes; Institutional workflows; Roles and responsibilities of assessors; Roles and responsibilities of institutions; and Learner support mechanisms. Learner support is expected to include areas such as: Guidance; Counselling; and Bridging mechanisms. This operational dimension is particularly important because it translates national policy into procedures that institutions and practitioners can actually follow. 6. Stakeholder Engagement and Co-Creation Stakeholder participation is a central component of the assignment. The consultant or consultancy firm will facilitate a structured consultation process involving a broad range of stakeholders. Government stakeholders are expected to include the relevant bodies responsible for education, higher education, labour, vocational training and curriculum development. Consultations will also involve: Private-sector organisations; Employers; Civil society organisations; Training providers; and Development partners. Development partners specifically identified in the Terms of Reference include organisations such as: International Labour Organization; UNESCO; Norwegian Refugee Council; and International Organization for Migration. Workshops will be conducted using in-person and/or hybrid formats to validate key elements of the proposed framework. This collaborative approach is intended to ensure that the resulting RPL framework reflects national realities, incorporates stakeholder expertise and develops sufficient ownership to support implementation and endorsement. 7. Finalisation and Government Endorsement Support After consultation, the consultant will incorporate relevant stakeholder feedback into the final framework. The consultant will also support the preparation of documentation suitable for endorsement and provide technical input for high-level validation or endorsement meetings. Consequently, the assignment covers the development process from policy analysis and system design through stakeholder consultation and final preparation for potential government endorsement. Expected Deliverables The consultant or consultancy firm will be responsible for producing a substantial set of deliverables. These include: Inception Report covering the methodology, workplan and stakeholder engagement plan. Draft National RPL Policy Framework . Institutional Architecture and Governance Model . Assessment and Certification Framework . Quality Assurance Framework . RPL Implementation Guidelines / Operational Manual . Consultation Reports summarising stakeholder contributions and inputs. Final National RPL Policy Framework , prepared in an endorsement-ready format. These deliverables demonstrate that the assignment requires expertise spanning policy development, technical design, institutional analysis, stakeholder engagement and practical implementation planning. Duration of the Consultancy The consultancy will run from contract signature until 31 March 2027 . Rather than being completed as a single continuous exercise, the work is expected to be organised around phased milestones aligned with stakeholder consultation and validation processes. The assignment has an estimated level of effort of up to 42 working days , distributed throughout the contract period. Those working days are intended to cover major deliverables, consultation activities and reporting responsibilities. Travel, Workshops and Operational Support Additional operational budget is allocated for workshops, consultations and stakeholder engagement. Approved consultant travel costs to Sudan, where travel is required and approved, will be handled separately through the operational provision. Importantly, travel to Sudan is subject to security assessments . The methodology also anticipates hybrid engagement arrangements combining remote and in-person consultations, reflecting the prevailing security context. Methodology Expected from the Consultant The successful consultant or firm is expected to use a methodology appropriate for complex policy and institutional reform. The British Council specifically expects: A co-creation and participatory approach ; A systems approach linking policy, institutions and implementation; Use of international best practices , including relevant ILO and UNESCO approaches and comparative RPL models; and Hybrid engagement modalities , incorporating remote and in-person consultation where appropriate. Applicants preparing their technical proposals should therefore pay close attention to these methodological expectations. The proposal should demonstrate not only what the applicant intends to deliver but also how the consultant or team will engage stakeholders, translate international experience into the Sudanese context and develop an implementable national framework. Reporting and Management Arrangements The selected consultant or consultancy firm will report to the Youth Skills Programme Manager, British Council Sudan . Technical coordination will also be maintained with relevant government stakeholders. The British Council will be responsible for overall contract management and logistical support associated with consultations. This arrangement means the consultant will need to operate effectively across technical, governmental and programme-management environments. Required Expertise and Experience Applicants should demonstrate strong and directly relevant expertise. The British Council requires proven experience in designing and implementing Recognition of Prior Learning systems or frameworks . Applicants should also demonstrate strong expertise in: Technical and Vocational Education and Training systems reform; Qualifications frameworks; Skills recognition; Non-formal education systems; and Related policy and institutional development. Experience working in fragile or conflict-affected contexts is another important requirement. Applicants should be capable of facilitating complex multi-stakeholder policy processes , given the significant consultation and co-creation responsibilities involved in the assignment. Familiarity with ILO, UNESCO or other international RPL standards is described as highly desirable. Additional Considerations for Consultancy Firms Consultancy firms interested in applying should consider the multidisciplinary nature of the assignment. For firms, a multidisciplinary team covering policy, assessment and institutional design is preferred . A strong team proposal should therefore demonstrate how the combined expertise of key personnel addresses the different technical components of the assignment. Application Requirements Interested individual consultants and consultancy firms are expected to submit several important documents. Applicants should prepare: Technical Proposal – explaining the proposed methodology and approach for undertaking the assignment. Financial Proposal – providing the financial proposal for delivering the consultancy. Relevant Experience and References – demonstrating previous experience related to the requirements of the assignment. CV(s) of Key Personnel – outlining the qualifications and professional experience of the consultant or proposed team members. The vacancy notice particularly emphasises that applicants should attach the technical proposal for developing the RPL Policy Framework together with their CV . Applicants should therefore carefully review the Terms of Reference and ensure their technical proposal addresses the assignment s expected methodology, scope, stakeholder engagement requirements, deliverables and implementation considerations. APPLY NOW Ethical Requirements The selected consultant or consultancy firm must comply with important ethical principles throughout the assignment. These include adherence to: Do no harm principles ; and Data protection and confidentiality standards . These requirements are especially significant considering the sensitive operating environment and the range of government, civil society, education-sector and development stakeholders expected to participate in the process. British Council RPL Consultant Application Deadline The closing date for applications is 26 August 2026 . Applicants should ensure that all required documents are prepared and submitted through the British Council recruitment system before the closing date. Application Deadline: 26 August 2026 Because the application requires more than a CV, prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare a strong technical proposal, financial proposal, evidence of relevant experience, references and CVs for relevant personnel. Important Points Applicants Should Remember Before applying for the British Council International Consultant – Recognition of Prior Learning opportunity, prospective applicants should take note of the following: The consultancy focuses on developing a National Recognition of Prior Learning Policy Framework for Sudan . The assignment requires substantial expertise in RPL systems and frameworks. Strong knowledge of TVET reform, qualifications frameworks, skills recognition and non-formal education is required. Experience in fragile or conflict-affected environments is expected. Applicants must be able to facilitate multi-stakeholder policy processes. Familiarity with ILO, UNESCO or international RPL standards is highly desirable. Consultancy firms preferably should propose multidisciplinary expertise covering policy, assessment and institutional design. The work involves policy development as well as practical implementation guidance. Stakeholder engagement and co-creation are central components of the assignment. The contract is expected to continue until 31 March 2027 . The estimated level of effort is up to 42 working days across the contract period. Engagement may involve both remote and in-person activities. Travel to Sudan, where approved, is subject to security assessments. Applicants must submit a technical proposal. A financial proposal is required. Relevant experience and references must be provided. CVs of key personnel must be submitted. The application deadline is 26 August 2026 . Conclusion The British Council International Consultant – Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) opportunity in Sudan provides experienced education, TVET, qualifications and policy specialists with an opportunity to contribute to an important national skills-system initiative. At the centre of the consultancy is the challenge of developing a Recognition of Prior Learning system capable of acknowledging competencies acquired through non-formal and informal pathways and connecting those competencies more effectively with recognised qualifications, education and employment opportunities. The assignment is particularly significant within Sudan s current context, where conflict, displacement, disrupted education and the dominance of informal economic activity have increased the importance of flexible and inclusive approaches to skills recognition. The successful consultant or consultancy firm will be expected to move beyond producing a high-level policy document. The work encompasses policy and legal considerations, institutional architecture, governance, competency assessment, certification, quality assurance, implementation guidance, stakeholder co-creation and support for final validation and endorsement. Professionals and consultancy firms with substantial experience in RPL systems, TVET reform, qualifications frameworks, non-formal education and multi-stakeholder policy development should carefully review the requirements and prepare comprehensive technical and financial proposals. title: RMIT University Research Fellow 2026: Apply for the Technology Adoption & Social Change Position in Melbourne, Australia
summary: RMIT University is inviting applications for an exciting Research Fellow in Technology Adoption Social Change position based in Melbourne, Australia. This four-year, full-time research appointment offers an opportunity for an appropriately qualified social sciences researcher to contribute to multidisciplinary research examining how people, workplaces and communities interact with emerging sensing technologies, artificial intelligence and complex data environments. The successful applicant will join the Technology Adoption and Social Change (TASC) program within the ARC Industrial Transformation Research Hub for Intelligent Contaminant-Sensing in Complex Environments (IC-SensE) . The position brings together social science, technology, artificial intelligence, industry collaboration and human-centred research, making it particularly relevant to researchers interested in the societal implications of emerging technologies. Based primarily at RMIT University s Melbourne CBD campus , the Research Fellow will conduct and contribute to high-quality research exploring consumer and workforce adoption of sensor technologies. The researcher will work alongside multidisciplinary academics and industry partners while investigating issues including socially responsible technology design, user experience, data security, trustworthy representation of data and AI-enabled workplace practices. title: University of British Columbia Four Year Doctoral Fellowship 2026: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity for International and Canadian Students
summary: The University of British Columbia (UBC) Four Year Doctoral Fellowship (4YF) is a major doctoral funding opportunity designed to support outstanding students undertaking advanced research at one of Canada s leading universities. The fellowship provides substantial financial support to eligible doctoral students, including international students, Canadian citizens, and permanent residents. Effective September 2026 onward , recipients of the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship can receive a $24,000 annual stipend plus full tuition coverage per year for up to four years of their doctoral studies. The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship program is intended to help UBC attract and retain exceptional doctoral researchers while giving recipients stable base-level financial support for their studies and research. One particularly important feature of the 4YF is its application process. Students do not normally submit a separate application specifically for the fellowship. Instead, PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who are offered admission to UBC are automatically considered for 4YF funding . For prospective doctoral students searching for UBC scholarships for international students, fully funded PhD opportunities in Canada, doctoral scholarships in Canada, UBC PhD funding, or Canadian scholarships for international doctoral students , the Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is an important funding opportunity to consider. UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship 2026 Overview Here are the major details prospective applicants should know: Host institution: The University of British Columbia (UBC) Campus: Vancouver Campus, Canada Program: Four Year Doctoral Fellowship (4YF) Degree level: Doctoral Eligible doctoral programs: PhD, DMA, and MDPhD Annual stipend: $24,000 Tuition: Full tuition coverage Maximum funding period: Up to four years Citizenship eligibility: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students Selection basis: Academic excellence and recommendation by the graduate program Application method: Apply for admission to an appropriate UBC graduate program Separate 4YF application: Generally not required for incoming applicants Deadline: Set individually by each UBC graduate program New funding level effective: September 2026 onward What Is the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship? The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship , commonly referred to as the 4YF , is a funding program established by the University of British Columbia to support high-achieving doctoral students. Doctoral education can require several years of intensive academic study, original research, laboratory or fieldwork, data collection, academic writing, and dissertation preparation. Stable funding can therefore be an important factor in allowing doctoral researchers to concentrate on their academic work. Through the 4YF program, UBC provides selected doctoral students with a combination of stipend funding and tuition support. The university describes the program as a mechanism that allows UBC to continue attracting and supporting outstanding domestic and international doctoral students while providing recipients with stable, base-level funding for their doctoral studies and research. UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Value Beginning September 2026 , the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship provides recipients with: $24,000 Annual Stipend Successful recipients can receive $24,000 in stipend funding per year . The stipend provides financial support while recipients undertake their doctoral studies and research. Full Tuition Coverage In addition to the $24,000 stipend, the fellowship provides tuition coverage . This makes the funding package particularly significant because the fellowship addresses both tuition expenses and provides a stipend. Funding for Up to Four Years The 4YF can provide funding for up to four years of doctoral study . However, applicants should understand that four years represents the potential maximum duration rather than a guarantee that every recipient will receive precisely four years of support. UBC states that the duration can be shorter in certain circumstances. Recipients should consult the official 4YF Guidelines for detailed policies governing the duration and administration of their funding. Funding is also subject to recipients maintaining satisfactory academic progress . How Much Could the UBC 4YF Be Worth Over Four Years? At the stated rate of $24,000 per year , a recipient funded at that stipend level for the full four years could receive up to $96,000 in stipend funding , in addition to applicable tuition coverage. The calculation is: $24,000 per year × 4 years = $96,000 in stipend funding The actual amount and duration received by an individual student can depend on their circumstances, funding period, other scholarships, academic standing, and the rules contained in UBC s Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Guidelines. Who Can Apply for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship? The UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is available to both domestic and international doctoral students . UBC states that Four Year Fellowships may be held by: Canadian students; Canadian permanent residents; and International students. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to international students seeking doctoral funding in Canada. There is no country-specific restriction stated in the supplied fellowship information. International students from different regions of the world may therefore be considered as long as they satisfy the relevant UBC doctoral admission requirements and other conditions of the program. Eligible Degree Programs The fellowship is generally offered to students beginning their first year of full-time study in one of the following types of doctoral programs: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) Combined MD/PhD (MDPhD) While incoming doctoral students are a major focus of the program, UBC states that Four Year Fellowships may also be offered to continuing students . Therefore, the fellowship is not necessarily restricted exclusively to new doctoral students. Priority for Incoming Doctoral Students Each UBC graduate program receives an allocation of Four Year Fellowships. Graduate programs assess their incoming and continuing doctoral students and select their strongest candidates for the available fellowships. According to UBC, priority is given to incoming students . Prospective doctoral candidates with excellent academic records should therefore pay particular attention to the admission requirements and deadlines of their intended graduate program, because applying for admission is also the route through which incoming candidates are considered for 4YF funding. UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Eligibility Requirements Although individual circumstances can vary, the major eligibility considerations include the following. 1. Applicants Should Be Pursuing an Eligible Doctoral Program The fellowship is generally intended for full-time students in PhD, DMA, or MDPhD programs. 2. Domestic and International Students Are Eligible The fellowship is not restricted to Canadian citizens. Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students can hold Four Year Fellowships. 3. Academic Excellence Is Essential UBC states that selection is based on academic excellence , following a recommendation from the student s graduate program. This means admission to a doctoral program does not automatically guarantee receipt of the fellowship. 4. Incoming Students Receive Priority Although continuing students may receive a 4YF, graduate programs give priority to incoming students when selecting recipients. 5. Recipients Must Maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress Continued funding is subject to satisfactory academic progress. Students who receive the fellowship should therefore familiarize themselves with the academic and administrative conditions attached to the award. Selection and Evaluation Criteria Selection for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is based on academic excellence . Recommendations are made through individual graduate programs. This means that the relevant graduate program plays an important role in identifying and recommending candidates for the fellowship. Because the number of fellowships allocated to each graduate program is limited, applicants should understand that simply satisfying UBC s minimum doctoral admission requirements does not necessarily mean they will receive a Four Year Fellowship. Graduate programs review eligible students and offer fellowships to their strongest candidates. How to Apply for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship The application process is relatively straightforward for prospective doctoral students because there is generally no separate 4YF application required from incoming applicants . Step 1: Identify an Appropriate UBC Graduate Program Prospective students should first identify a PhD, DMA, or MDPhD program at the University of British Columbia that aligns with their academic background and research interests. Students planning a research degree may also wish to investigate potential faculty supervisors whose research interests correspond with their proposed area of study. Step 2: Review the Graduate Program s Admission Requirements Admission requirements can vary between UBC graduate programs. Applicants should carefully review the requirements of the particular program they intend to enter, including academic qualifications, supporting documents, research requirements, language requirements where applicable, and any program-specific conditions. Step 3: Check the Program-Specific Application Deadline This step is especially important because there is no single university-wide 4YF deadline listed for applicants . The deadline is set by each UBC graduate program . Applicants must therefore check the application deadline for their chosen graduate program and ensure their admission application is submitted on time. Step 4: Apply for Admission to UBC To be considered for Four Year Fellowship funding, prospective students submit an application for admission to the appropriate UBC graduate program. Step 5: Automatic Consideration for 4YF Funding All PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who are offered admission are automatically considered for Four Year Fellowship funding . This means applicants generally do not need to prepare and submit an additional standalone application for the 4YF itself. Step 6: Graduate Programs Select Their Strongest Candidates Each graduate program receives an allocation of Four Year Fellowships and reviews incoming and continuing students. The programs then offer the fellowships to their strongest candidates, with priority given to incoming students. For information about admission procedures and requirements visit the Application Admission page. APPLY NOW UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Deadline There is no single deadline for the Four Year Doctoral Fellowship . Deadline: Set by each UBC graduate program. Prospective applicants should not interpret the absence of a universal deadline as meaning that applications can be submitted at any time. Instead, applicants must check the admission deadline for the specific doctoral program to which they wish to apply. Since admission to an eligible graduate program is the route through which incoming students are considered for 4YF funding, missing the relevant graduate admission deadline could also mean missing the opportunity to be considered for the fellowship for that admission cycle. Applicants should therefore verify the current deadline directly through UBC s official graduate program and admission pages. Nomination Process The nomination process is primarily handled internally by UBC graduate programs rather than by applicants themselves. Each graduate program receives a certain number of Four Year Fellowships each year. Programs review both incoming and continuing students and select their strongest students, with incoming students receiving priority. After selecting a recipient, the graduate program notifies UBC Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies by submitting a signed University Award Recommendation Form . For administrative purposes, the program uses award number 6456 . UBC states that it is not necessary to list an award amount on the recommendation form. Recommendation forms should be submitted at least eight weeks before the requested 4YF start date . This eight-week timeframe concerns the university s nomination/recommendation process and should not be confused with the student s graduate admission deadline. Tri-Agency Award Holders and the 4YF The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship also interacts with several major Canadian research awards. Students holding certain Tri-Agency awards automatically become 4YF designates . These include: Vanier Scholarships; Doctoral Canada Graduate Scholarships (CGSD); Canadian Institutes of Health Research Doctoral Research Awards; Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council Doctoral Postgraduate Scholarships (PGSD); and Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council Doctoral Fellowships. Doctoral students who receive qualifying Tri-Agency scholarships may be eligible for 4YF tuition coverage . They can also receive 4YF stipend and tuition support after their external scholarship funding ends, subject to the applicable time limits. According to the information provided by UBC, this support can continue until four years after the external award start date or until the end of the student s fifth year in the doctoral program, whichever occurs first . Other Major External Scholarship Winners The 4YF can also interact with other major external scholarships. Recipients of major external scholarships who are selected as 4YF designates may be eligible for tuition coverage through the 4YF. They may subsequently receive 4YF stipend and tuition support after their external scholarship funding concludes. For these recipients, funding can continue until four years after the 4YF start date or until the end of their fifth year in the doctoral program, whichever occurs first . Students receiving external funding should carefully review UBC s official 4YF Guidelines to understand how their external scholarship interacts with their Four Year Fellowship designation. Important Funding Requirement for 4YF Holders Receiving a Four Year Doctoral Fellowship does not necessarily mean students can ignore other external funding opportunities. UBC requires 4YF holders to apply for other funding in order to maintain their eligibility for 4YF funding . The requirements differ depending on the student s status. Canadian Citizens and Permanent Residents 4YF holders who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents must apply for Tri-Agency funding every year when eligible . This is an important condition. UBC states that eligible Canadian citizens or permanent residents who fail to apply for the required Tri-Agency funding will forfeit their remaining 4YF funding . Recipients should therefore take this requirement seriously and keep track of relevant external scholarship competitions and deadlines. International Students International 4YF recipients are not required to apply to the annual Affiliated Fellowship competition, which is held each fall. However, international recipients are eligible to enter the competition if they choose. Doing so may provide an opportunity to compete for Affiliated Fellowships carrying higher stipend amounts, including opportunities such as the Killam Doctoral Fellowship . Can 4YF Funding Be Interrupted? UBC provides a mechanism through which 4YF payments can be interrupted for certain non-academic reasons. Examples given by the university include: Relevant work experience; and Paid internships. UBC provides a 4YF Interruption Form for recipients who need such an interruption and who do not intend to apply for a corresponding professional leave of absence from the university. Because interruptions can affect fellowship payments and potentially the administration of an award, recipients considering this option should consult UBC s official rules and relevant graduate program before making arrangements. Why the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Is an Important Opportunity The UBC 4YF stands out because it combines several significant benefits. Substantial Annual Financial Support A $24,000 annual stipend provides recipients with a meaningful base level of financial support during their doctoral studies. Tuition Coverage The fellowship also provides tuition coverage, reducing one of the major educational costs associated with completing a doctoral degree. Potential Four-Year Duration Funding may be available for up to four years, providing a degree of financial stability over a substantial portion of a recipient s doctoral studies. International Students Are Eligible International students can be considered alongside Canadian citizens and permanent residents, making the fellowship relevant to doctoral candidates worldwide. No Separate Fellowship Application for Incoming Applicants Eligible PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who receive an offer of admission are automatically considered for 4YF funding. This reduces the need to complete a separate fellowship application during the initial admission process. Broad Research Possibilities at UBC The examples of current and previous award holders provided by UBC illustrate the breadth of research supported through doctoral study at the university. Research represented among featured fellowship holders includes areas such as: Microbiology and immunology; Interdisciplinary studies; Zoology; Biochemistry and molecular biology; Oceanography; Population and public health; Gender, race, sexuality and social justice; School and applied child psychology; Resources, environment and sustainability; and Cell and developmental biology. These examples demonstrate that the Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is not confined to one narrow academic discipline. Important Points Applicants Should Remember Prospective applicants should keep several important details in mind: Apply for admission first. Incoming applicants are considered for the 4YF through their application to an eligible UBC doctoral program. There is no universal deadline. The deadline is determined by each graduate program, so applicants need to check the deadline for their chosen program. Admission does not guarantee a fellowship. Applicants offered admission are automatically considered, but individual graduate programs select their strongest candidates from the eligible pool. Academic excellence is central to selection. The fellowship is intended to support outstanding doctoral students. Incoming students receive priority. Continuing students may receive a fellowship, but UBC states that priority is given to incoming students. International students are eligible. The program is open to international students as well as Canadian citizens and permanent residents. Funding can last up to four years. However, the actual funding period can be shorter depending on individual circumstances and the applicable 4YF policies. Academic progress matters. Fellowship funding remains subject to satisfactory academic progress. Other funding obligations may apply. In particular, eligible Canadian citizens and permanent residents holding a 4YF must apply annually for Tri-Agency funding to retain their remaining 4YF eligibility. Recipients should read the official 4YF Guidelines. Detailed rules concerning the administration, duration, interruption, and interaction of 4YF funding with other awards are contained in UBC s official guidelines. How Prospective Applicants Can Strengthen Their Position Because selection is based on academic excellence and graduate-program recommendation, prospective students should focus on submitting the strongest possible application for admission. Applicants should carefully demonstrate their academic preparation, research potential, relevant experience, and suitability for their proposed doctoral program wherever these elements are requested as part of the admission process. For research-focused degrees, identifying appropriate faculty expertise and understanding the research environment of the intended graduate program can also be an important part of preparing a competitive doctoral application. Applicants should always follow the specific instructions issued by their chosen UBC program because requirements can vary across departments and disciplines. Final Reminder About the Deadline The UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship does not have one universal application deadline . Deadline: Set by each UBC graduate program. Prospective students should locate their intended PhD, DMA, or MDPhD program on UBC s official graduate website, confirm its current admission deadline, and submit all required admission materials according to that program s instructions. Applicants should avoid relying on deadlines associated with unrelated UBC programs because different graduate programs may operate according to different application schedules. Conclusion The University of British Columbia Four Year Doctoral Fellowship (4YF) represents a significant funding opportunity for outstanding students seeking doctoral education in Canada. With $24,000 in annual stipend funding plus tuition coverage for up to four years , the fellowship can provide recipients with substantial financial support while they pursue advanced research at UBC. Its accessibility to Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and international students makes the program particularly noteworthy for prospective doctoral candidates worldwide. Moreover, eligible PhD, DMA, and MDPhD applicants who are offered admission are automatically considered for the fellowship, meaning there is generally no separate 4YF application for incoming students. Competition should nevertheless be expected. Fellowships are allocated among UBC graduate programs, and programs select their strongest students based on academic excellence, with priority given to incoming candidates. Anyone interested in the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship 2026 should begin by identifying an appropriate UBC doctoral program, carefully reviewing its admission requirements, checking its specific application deadline, and preparing a strong application for admission. Most importantly, prospective applicants should remember that the deadline is determined by each UBC graduate program . Applicants should therefore consult the official University of British Columbia Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies website and their chosen graduate program for the latest admission requirements, deadlines, funding policies, and Four Year Doctoral Fellowship guidelines before applying.
