title: COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon 2026 in Türkiye: Apply to Develop Climate Solutions and Join the International COP31 Ideathon in Antalya
summary: The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is inviting young people across Türkiye to turn their climate ideas into practical solutions for some of the most urgent environmental challenges facing communities and the planet. Organized under the Turkish Ministry of Youth and Sports , the initiative provides young participants with an intensive opportunity to work in multidisciplinary teams, receive guidance from expert mentors, develop solutions to real environmental problems and present their ideas before a jury. The programme is particularly designed for young people interested in climate change, sustainability, environmental protection, zero waste and the circular economy . Participants will spend three days working collaboratively on a selected climate-related challenge, with the strongest teams potentially advancing to an international ideathon in Antalya held alongside the COP31 process. The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon offers an opportunity not only to develop an innovative climate solution but also to connect with young people from different parts of Türkiye and, for successful teams, eventually collaborate with participants from countries around the world. About the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is a youth-focused climate innovation and solution-development initiative designed to give young people an active role in responding to climate change. Rather than simply discussing the environmental challenges facing society, participants are encouraged to identify problems and develop original, practical and feasible solutions . The programme brings together young people from different cities and disciplines and places them in collaborative teams. With support from expert mentors, participants will work through a three-day ideathon experience to transform their initial ideas into more developed solutions. The initiative is connected to the broader COP31 process , creating a potential pathway for successful youth teams to take their solutions to an international platform in Antalya. The programme s underlying message is that young people should not only be consulted about the climate crisis but should also have opportunities to design and develop solutions that can contribute to the future of environmental policy and action. What Is an Ideathon? An ideathon is an intensive, collaborative problem-solving event in which participants work together to develop innovative responses to a particular challenge. In the case of the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon, participants will: Select or be assigned a climate-related theme. Work in multidisciplinary youth teams. Examine a real environmental problem. Generate and refine potential solutions. Receive guidance from expert mentors. Develop a feasible solution proposal. Present their idea to a jury. Compete for the opportunity to progress to the international stage. The format encourages participants to move beyond general awareness of climate change and focus on solutions that can realistically address environmental challenges . What Participants Can Expect Selected participants will take part in a three-day experience focused on climate solution development. Three Days of Collaborative Solution Development Participants will work with their teams for three days to address a real environmental problem. The experience is intended to strengthen practical skills such as: Problem identification Research Critical thinking Creative thinking Collaboration Communication Solution design Presentation Project development Teamwork Participants will have the opportunity to turn an initial concept into a more structured and potentially implementable climate solution. Expert Mentorship Participants will receive one-on-one support from expert mentors working in relevant fields. Mentors can help participants: Evaluate their ideas. Identify weaknesses in proposed solutions. Improve feasibility. Develop stronger approaches to environmental problems. Think about implementation. Prepare their final presentations. This mentorship component is particularly valuable because participants are not expected to develop their ideas entirely on their own. Presentation Before a Jury At the end of the ideathon experience, teams will have the opportunity to present their ideas to a jury. This gives participants practical experience in communicating an environmental solution to decision-makers and experts. Teams will need to demonstrate not only that their idea is innovative but also that it can potentially address a genuine environmental challenge. Youth Networking The initiative will bring together young people from different cities across Türkiye. Participants can therefore build connections with peers who share interests in: Climate action Sustainability Environmental protection Renewable energy Circular economy Climate leadership Green transition The multidisciplinary nature of the programme can also help participants discover perspectives and approaches outside their usual academic or professional areas. Opportunity to Participate in the International Ideathon in Antalya One of the most significant opportunities associated with the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is the possibility of progressing to the international stage. Teams that perform particularly well may have the opportunity to participate in the international ideathon in Antalya during the COP31 process. At the international ideathon, successful teams will have the opportunity to: Develop their ideas on an international scale. Work alongside young participants from different countries. Exchange ideas across national and cultural contexts. Further refine their proposed solutions. Present their work on an international platform. Contribute to discussions connected with global climate challenges. This creates a potential progression from a local or national youth ideathon to an international climate innovation experience. COP31 and the International Climate Context The initiative is connected to the COP31 process , giving the programme an important international climate-policy dimension. The United Nations Climate Change Conference, commonly known as COP, brings countries together to discuss international action on climate change. The COP31-related youth initiative seeks to create space for young people to contribute their own ideas and solutions to environmental challenges. For participants, this can provide valuable exposure to the broader climate policy and sustainability ecosystem. Eight Climate and Sustainability Themes Participants will develop ideas under one of eight thematic areas. These themes cover a broad range of environmental, social and economic dimensions of climate action. 1. Green Skills and Climate Literacy This theme focuses on strengthening the knowledge and skills people need to understand and respond to climate change. Potential ideas could address: Climate education Environmental awareness Green skills development Youth climate education Sustainability training Climate communication Environmental literacy Young people interested in education, training and awareness-raising may find this theme particularly relevant. 2. Youth Participation and Climate Leadership This theme focuses on increasing young people s involvement in climate action and environmental decision-making. Possible areas of interest include: Youth participation Climate leadership Youth-led environmental initiatives Climate advocacy Youth representation Community engagement Environmental policymaking The theme recognizes young people as active contributors to climate solutions rather than passive beneficiaries of environmental policies. 3. Adaptation and Resilience to Climate Change Climate change is already affecting communities and ecosystems, making adaptation and resilience increasingly important. Participants working on this theme may explore solutions related to: Climate adaptation Disaster preparedness Community resilience Climate risk management Resilient infrastructure Local adaptation strategies Protection of vulnerable communities The emphasis is on developing approaches that can help communities prepare for and respond to climate-related risks. 4. Air Pollution, Clean Air and the Green Transition Air pollution represents both an environmental and public-health challenge. This theme invites ideas addressing: Air quality Pollution reduction Clean transportation Clean energy Sustainable urban development Green technologies Low-carbon transition Participants can explore innovative ways to reduce pollution while supporting a broader transition toward more sustainable systems. 5. Combating Forest Fires, Drought and Water Stress This theme addresses environmental challenges that can become more severe as climate conditions change. Participants may develop solutions relating to: Forest-fire prevention Early warning systems Drought management Water conservation Water security Climate-resilient ecosystems Community preparedness The theme is particularly relevant to innovative approaches that help communities and ecosystems cope with increasing environmental pressures. 6. Agriculture and Food Security Climate change has significant implications for agriculture and food systems. Ideas under this theme could explore: Climate-smart agriculture Sustainable farming Food security Agricultural resilience Efficient water use Sustainable food systems Reducing environmental impacts of agriculture Participants can examine how food systems can become more resilient while contributing to environmental sustainability. 7. Renewable Energy and Carbon Footprint Reduction This theme focuses on the transition toward cleaner energy systems and reducing greenhouse-gas emissions. Potential areas include: Renewable energy Solar energy Energy efficiency Low-carbon technologies Carbon footprint reduction Clean energy access Sustainable consumption Participants with interests in engineering, technology, energy or environmental science may find this theme particularly suitable. 8. Youth-Friendly and Environmentally Friendly Sports Facilities The final theme connects climate action with sports and youth facilities. Participants may explore how sports facilities can become: More environmentally sustainable More energy efficient More accessible to young people Less carbon intensive More resource efficient Better integrated into sustainable communities This theme demonstrates that climate action can be incorporated into many aspects of everyday community life. Learn More Who Can Apply? The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is aimed specifically at young people between 15 and 29 years old . Applicants should have an interest in at least one of the areas connected to the programme, including: Climate change Sustainability Environmental protection Zero waste Circular economy Applicants do not need to be described as climate experts. The initiative is designed to give young people an opportunity to develop ideas with the support of mentors and other participants. The multidisciplinary nature of the programme means that young people with different educational, professional and personal backgrounds may be able to contribute. Nationality and Geographic Eligibility The programme information states that young people will be selected from across Türkiye and that the in-person ideathon events will take place in cities across Türkiye. Therefore, this opportunity is primarily intended for young people in Türkiye , particularly those eligible to participate through the Turkish Ministry of Youth and Sports E-Genç platform. The information provided does not indicate that applicants from other countries can directly apply to the national ideathon stages. However, participants whose teams successfully advance may have the opportunity to take part in the international ideathon in Antalya , where they can work alongside participants from different countries. International participation therefore appears to be associated with the later stage of the programme rather than the initial national application. Where Will the Ideathon Take Place? The national ideathon is scheduled to take place in seven cities across Türkiye . Istanbul 4–6 September 2026 Rize 9–11 September 2026 Adana 18–20 September 2026 Konya 25–27 September 2026 Izmir 2–4 October 2026 Mardin 9–11 October 2026 Erzurum 16–18 October 2026 Applicants should pay close attention to the location and dates relevant to their participation. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the E-Genç Platform , the youth-focused digital platform associated with the Turkish Ministry of Youth and Sports. During the application process, applicants are expected to provide a short solution proposal addressing one of the eight programme themes. A strong proposal should focus on a specific environmental or climate challenge and present a solution that is: Original Practical Feasible Relevant to the selected theme Potentially useful to communities Capable of being developed further during the ideathon Applicants should avoid presenting only a general statement about climate change. The purpose of the application is to demonstrate an ability to identify a problem and begin thinking about a realistic solution. APPLY HERE! What Makes a Strong Solution Proposal? Although the programme emphasizes creativity and innovation, a successful idea should also demonstrate practical thinking. Applicants can strengthen their proposals by considering questions such as: What is the problem? Clearly identify the climate or environmental challenge. For example, instead of simply discussing water scarcity, identify a particular aspect of water stress affecting communities. Who is affected? Explain the people, communities, ecosystems or sectors affected by the problem. What is your proposed solution? Describe the core idea clearly and simply. Why is the solution different? Explain what makes the proposal innovative or different from existing approaches. Is it feasible? Consider whether the solution could realistically be implemented with available or potentially accessible resources. What impact could it create? Explain how the proposed solution could improve environmental, social or community outcomes. Multidisciplinary Teams The programme places particular importance on teams made up of young people from different disciplines . This approach recognizes that complex climate challenges rarely have a single solution or belong to one academic field. For example, a climate solution might benefit from combining: Environmental science Engineering Economics Technology Agriculture Communications Public policy Business Education Design Participants will therefore have opportunities to learn from people with different knowledge, skills and perspectives. From Idea to Implementation The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon is designed to take participants beyond simply generating ideas. The three-day experience allows teams to develop their proposals through: Problem identification. Idea generation. Team discussion. Expert mentoring. Solution refinement. Feasibility consideration. Presentation preparation. Jury evaluation. The strongest teams can then potentially take their ideas to the international stage in Antalya. This progression gives participants an opportunity to see how an initial concept can evolve into a more developed climate solution. Benefits of Participating The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon offers several potential benefits for young participants. Practical Climate Innovation Experience Participants gain hands-on experience developing solutions to real environmental challenges. Expert Mentorship One-on-one guidance provides participants with access to experienced professionals who can help improve their ideas. Networking Participants can establish relationships with young people from different cities and potentially, at the international stage, from different countries. Presentation Skills Presenting before a jury can strengthen participants ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and persuasively. Teamwork Participants gain experience collaborating with people from different disciplines and backgrounds. Exposure to International Climate Action Successful teams may have the opportunity to participate in an international ideathon connected with the COP31 process. Contribution to Environmental Policy and Action The programme encourages young people to develop ideas that could potentially contribute to future environmental policies and climate solutions. Why Young People Should Consider Applying Climate change presents complex challenges requiring innovation across multiple sectors. Young people are often among the most affected by long-term environmental changes, but they also bring new perspectives, technologies and approaches to solving these problems. The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon provides a structured environment where young people can turn those perspectives into practical proposals. The programme can be particularly valuable for young people interested in building experience in: Climate policy Environmental science Sustainability Renewable energy Circular economy Agriculture Environmental technology Climate leadership Public policy Green innovation Community development Application Deadline The information provided for the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon does not state a specific application closing date . Applications are currently presented as open through the E-Genç Platform . Applicants should therefore check the official application portal for the current submission deadline and complete their applications as early as possible. The scheduled national ideathon events begin on 4 September 2026 in Istanbul , followed by events in Rize, Adana, Konya, Izmir, Mardin and Erzurum through October 2026. Organizing Institution The initiative is regulated by the: Turkish Ministry of Youth and Sports Address: Örnek Mahallesi, Oruç Reis Caddesi No:13, Altındağ, Ankara, Türkiye The Ministry operates the youth-focused platforms and programmes through which participants can access information and submit applications. Important Information for Applicants Before applying, candidates should: Confirm that they meet the 15–29 age requirement . Review the eight available climate themes. Select a theme that matches their interests and strengths. Develop a clear and practical climate solution. Prepare the requested short solution proposal. Submit the application through the E-Genç Platform. Check the application portal for the latest deadline and participation details. Consider the location and dates of the relevant ideathon event. Be prepared to collaborate in a multidisciplinary team. Be available for the full three-day ideathon experience if selected. Visit HERE to learn more about the COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon 2026 in Türkiye. Conclusion The COP31 Youth Climate Ideathon provides young people in Türkiye with an opportunity to move from climate awareness to practical climate action. Through three days of intensive teamwork, expert mentorship and solution development, participants can explore real environmental challenges and transform their ideas into more feasible and impactful proposals. The programme covers eight major areas, ranging from climate literacy and youth leadership to renewable energy, agriculture, food security, water stress, air pollution, forest fires and sustainable sports facilities. This broad thematic scope means that young people with different interests and backgrounds can contribute to the climate solution-building process. One of the programme s most attractive features is the potential pathway to the international ideathon in Antalya . Teams that perform particularly well may have the opportunity to work with participants from countries around the world and develop their ideas within an international COP31-related environment. Young people aged 15 to 29 in Türkiye who are passionate about climate change, sustainability, environmental protection, zero waste or the circular economy should consider preparing a strong solution proposal and applying through the E-Genç Platform. Because the information provided does not specify a final application closing date, prospective applicants should consult the official platform promptly for the latest deadline and application requirements. title: Fully Funded PhD Position in Social Data Science at VU Amsterdam: Research the Online Manipulation Economy
summary: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, commonly known as VU Amsterdam, is accepting applications for a fully funded PhD Position in Social Data Science. This four-year doctoral opportunity will allow the successful candidate to investigate the market infrastructure behind disinformation, fake online engagement, bot networks and other forms of digital influence operations. The position is connected to the Vidi-funded research project titled “The Economy of Digital Influence Operations,” led by Associate Professor Jon Roozenbeek. The project moves beyond studying individual pieces of misinformation to examine the broader economic system that makes large-scale online manipulation possible. The successful candidate will join the Department of Communication Science within the Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities at VU Amsterdam. The doctoral researcher will use advanced quantitative research methods, social-media data, financial information, experiments and qualitative interviews to investigate how the online manipulation economy operates. This is a full-time, salaried doctoral position based primarily in Amsterdam, the Netherlands. The preferred starting date is 4 January 2027, and the selected candidate can receive a salary that rises to a maximum of €4,051 gross per month in the fourth year. According to the official VU Amsterdam vacancy announcement , applications must be submitted no later than Monday, 14 September 2026 at 23:59. Key Details About the VU Amsterdam PhD Position Host institution: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam Faculty: Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities Department: Department of Communication Science Research field: Social Data Science Research project: The Economy of Digital Influence Operations Location: VU Main Building, Amsterdam, the Netherlands Employment level: 1.0 full-time equivalent Working hours: 38 hours per week Duration: Four years, subject to a satisfactory first-year evaluation Starting salary: €3,204 gross per month Maximum fourth-year salary: €4,051 gross per month Preferred starting date: Monday, 4 January 2027 Application deadline: Monday, 14 September 2026 at 23:59 Expected interview period: 21–30 September 2026 Interview format: In Amsterdam or online Required educational level: Master’s degree Application language: English or Dutch Application method: Online through the official VU Amsterdam recruitment portal VU Amsterdam does not identify a timezone beside the deadline on the vacancy page. Applicants should therefore submit their materials well before 23:59 rather than waiting until the final hours. About the Economy of Digital Influence Operations Research Project Disinformation and coordinated online manipulation are often examined by focusing on misleading posts, individual social-media users or specific political campaigns. However, large-scale influence operations require more than misleading content. They depend on an extensive market in which fake accounts, automated engagement, artificial followers and sophisticated bot networks can be created, purchased and deployed. The “Economy of Digital Influence Operations” project will investigate this underlying market infrastructure. Through the project, the doctoral researcher will help map what the research team describes as the “online manipulation economy.” This includes examining the individuals, businesses, intermediaries and organizations involved in buying and selling digital manipulation services. The research may explore questions such as: Who creates and sells fake social-media accounts, automated engagement and bot networks? Who purchases these digital influence services, and what objectives do buyers hope to achieve? What economic, political or social motivations encourage individuals and organizations to participate in the market? How are buyers and sellers connected across digital platforms and national borders? What financial systems or transaction structures support the market? How do fake accounts and bot networks affect online discussions, public trust, political communication and democratic participation? What interventions could disrupt the supply of manipulation services? How can policymakers, researchers and technology companies develop system-level responses to coordinated digital influence operations? The project is supported by a Vidi grant awarded to Jon Roozenbeek. The wider research programme is intended to improve understanding of the black market that enables misleading information and political manipulation to spread online. More information about the grant and its research objectives is available through the official VU Amsterdam Vidi project announcement . Why This Social Data Science Research Matters Disinformation can threaten electoral integrity, weaken confidence in institutions, distort public debate and make it more difficult for citizens to distinguish authentic public opinion from coordinated manipulation. Many existing interventions concentrate on individuals. These may include warning labels, fact-checking services, media-literacy programmes or prompts that encourage users to assess information more carefully. Although these measures can be useful, their ability to stop large and organized influence operations may be limited. The VU Amsterdam project approaches the problem at a system level. Instead of looking only at the people who encounter misinformation, the research will investigate the commercial and technical infrastructure that allows manipulation campaigns to operate. Understanding this infrastructure could help researchers and policymakers identify more effective interventions. For example, evidence about sellers, buyers, payment systems and digital platforms could support new regulatory policies or enforcement strategies designed to reduce the availability of fake engagement services and automated influence networks. The PhD candidate will therefore contribute to research with potential importance for: Democratic institutions and electoral integrity Digital platform governance Online trust and safety Public policy and technology regulation Political communication Cybersecurity and information integrity Computational social science Social-media research Disinformation prevention Artificial intelligence and automated online behaviour Main Responsibilities of the PhD Candidate The successful applicant will complete a cumulative doctoral dissertation within four years. Rather than producing only one traditional monograph, the candidate will work on multiple connected academic studies that collectively address the objectives of the research project. The main responsibilities are expected to include the following. 1. Planning and Conducting Empirical Research The candidate will work with the supervisory team to plan and execute empirical studies on digital influence operations and the economic infrastructure supporting them. This work will require the researcher to turn broad theoretical questions into measurable research designs, determine what evidence is required and select suitable methods for collecting and analysing that evidence. 2. Designing Experiments Experimental research will form part of the doctoral project. The candidate may design studies that test the effects of online manipulation, evaluate potential interventions or examine how individuals and institutions respond to inauthentic online activity. Applicants should therefore be comfortable developing controlled research designs, identifying appropriate variables, formulating hypotheses and interpreting experimental results. 3. Collecting and Analysing Social-Media and Financial Data An important part of the position involves developing bespoke data pipelines for collecting and analysing relevant information. The candidate may work with large volumes of social-media data to identify coordinated behaviour, patterns of artificial engagement or networks of suspicious accounts. Financial or transactional data may also be used to understand the economic connections between buyers, sellers and service providers. Applicants should be prepared to work with complex, imperfect and potentially large datasets. 4. Conducting Qualitative Interviews Although the position requires strong quantitative skills, the project will not be limited to numerical data. Interviews with individuals who understand or participate in the online manipulation economy may provide essential information about motivations, business models and market practices that cannot be observed from platform data alone. The candidate may therefore contribute to identifying interview participants, designing interview protocols, conducting interviews and integrating qualitative findings with quantitative results. 5. Developing Reproducible Data Pipelines The successful applicant will help create tailored research pipelines using tools such as Python and R. These pipelines may be used to collect, clean, organize, connect and analyse information from several sources. Because the project follows open-science principles, the candidate will be expected to make research procedures, code, materials and eligible datasets reproducible and publicly accessible where appropriate and legally possible. 6. Publishing Research Findings The candidate will be expected to produce high-quality academic publications. Research findings may be presented through: Articles in leading international academic journals International conference papers and presentations Conference proceedings Public-facing research reports Policy briefs Online research resources Reproducible datasets, code and methodological materials The ability to communicate complex technical findings to both academic and non-academic audiences will be important. 7. Supporting Public-Facing Research Outputs The position may involve building and maintaining public resources similar to the Cambridge Online Trust and Safety Index . This responsibility reflects the project’s commitment to producing research outputs that are useful beyond traditional academic publications. Public-facing tools can help policymakers, technology professionals, civil-society organizations and the wider public understand online trust and safety challenges. 8. Participating in Doctoral Training The candidate will take part in courses and professional-development activities offered by the Graduate School of Social Sciences. This training is intended to support the candidate’s development in research methods, academic writing, research integrity, open science and other skills required to complete the doctorate successfully. Additional information is available through the VU Amsterdam Graduate School doctoral information page . 9. Building an International Research Network The doctoral researcher will be encouraged to collaborate with specialists working in communication science, psychology, computational social science, computer science, political communication, economics and related areas. The position will be based primarily at VU Amsterdam but will include close research connections with the University of Cambridge. Educational Qualifications Applicants should have completed a research master’s degree or another relevant master’s degree in a field such as: Social Data Science Communication Science Psychology Economics A closely related discipline that provides suitable quantitative and computational research training VU Amsterdam indicates a preference for candidates with excellent academic results, particularly strong performance on their final-year dissertation or master’s thesis. Applicants should use their application materials to demonstrate how their graduate education has prepared them to conduct independent, interdisciplinary research involving digital platforms, online information and advanced data analysis. Essential Technical and Research Skills This position requires a substantial quantitative and computational foundation. Competitive applicants should be able to demonstrate the following: Strong quantitative research abilities Applicants should understand how to design and conduct quantitative empirical research. This includes formulating research questions, selecting appropriate methods, evaluating evidence and interpreting results responsibly. Advanced statistical knowledge Candidates should have experience with advanced statistical analysis. Knowledge of time-series analysis is specifically identified as important for the position. Depending on the final studies developed during the project, other useful knowledge could include experimental analysis, regression modelling, network analysis, causal inference or computational text analysis. Programming experience in both Python and R Experience with Python and R is essential. Applicants should not assume that knowledge of only one of the two languages will meet the stated requirement. The candidate may use these programming languages to: Collect information through APIs or other permitted sources Clean and restructure complex datasets Conduct statistical analysis Build reproducible research pipelines Perform time-series or network analysis Produce visualizations Document analytical workflows Share code under open-science practices Research-design experience The candidate must be able to translate conceptual questions into rigorous empirical studies. Experience designing experiments or other structured research projects will therefore be valuable. Academic writing in English Excellent English academic-writing skills are essential. The successful candidate will need to prepare journal manuscripts, conference papers, dissertation chapters, public reports and research documentation. Interest in digital influence operations Applicants should show a clear intellectual interest in: The spread of information and misinformation online Fake or coordinated social-media activity Bot networks and automated engagement Digital influence operations The market infrastructure behind inauthentic content Platform governance and online trust The social and political effects of manipulation campaigns Russian or Mandarin language ability Knowledge of Russian and/or Mandarin would be an advantage, particularly because digital influence operations can involve actors and data from different linguistic environments. However, Russian and Mandarin are listed as desirable rather than mandatory. Applicants without these language skills may still apply if they satisfy the essential requirements. Personal Qualities VU Amsterdam Is Seeking The university is looking for more than technical competence. The successful candidate should also be: Sociable, open-minded and friendly Communicative and able to explain ideas clearly Responsible and capable of taking ownership of individual studies Diligent and conscientious Comfortable working independently Able to collaborate across academic disciplines Capable of communicating findings clearly in writing and conversation Prepared to work with colleagues in Amsterdam and Cambridge Independent working ability is especially important because lead supervisor Jon Roozenbeek spends part of the year at the University of Cambridge. Virtual supervisory meetings will be available, but the candidate must be able to organize research tasks, maintain progress and take responsibility for day-to-day project development. Supervisory Team and International Research Links The candidate will be supervised by Associate Professor Jon Roozenbeek and Ivar Vermeulen. Jon Roozenbeek leads the Vidi-funded research project and directs work within the Influence and Technology Lab. His research focuses on misinformation, online influence, digital technology and interventions designed to improve the quality of information environments. The project has close connections with research conducted at VU Amsterdam and the University of Cambridge. This arrangement gives the candidate an opportunity to work in an international research environment and develop professional relationships across institutions. Although some supervisory interaction may take place virtually, applicants should understand that the position itself is based primarily at VU Amsterdam. It is not advertised as a fully remote doctoral position. Salary and Employment Conditions The successful applicant will be employed by VU Amsterdam as a full-time doctoral researcher. The advertised salary begins at €3,204 gross per month and increases to a maximum of €4,051 gross per month in the fourth year, based on full-time employment and the applicable Dutch university employment conditions. The initial employment contract will be for one year. After a satisfactory evaluation, the contract can be extended so that the total appointment covers four years. The first-year evaluation will be based on progress and academic outputs defined through the Graduate School of Social Sciences. Applicants should recognize that the extension is dependent on satisfactory performance rather than being completely automatic. The doctoral dissertation is expected to be completed by the end of the fourth year, at which point the employment contract will end. Additional employment benefits include: A standard full-time working week of 38 hours 232 hours of annual leave based on a 38-hour working week An additional 96 hours of annual leave when working a 40-hour schedule Holiday allowance of 8% Year-end bonus of 8.3% A contribution toward commuting expenses Access to an optional personalized benefits package Access to university sports facilities for a modest fee Applicants should remember that the published salary figures are gross amounts. The final net salary will depend on Dutch taxation, social contributions and the successful candidate’s personal circumstances. About the Influence and Technology Lab The doctoral candidate will become part of the Influence and Technology Lab, an interdisciplinary research environment examining how information, technology and psychological processes influence what people believe and share. The lab combines knowledge and methods from areas including: Communication science Psychology Computer science Social data science Area studies Political communication Online trust and safety Its researchers use advanced social and computational methods to study information environments, propaganda, technology effects and interventions. The lab also has a cross-cultural orientation. It conducts research across countries and combines methodological rigour with attention to local political, linguistic and cultural contexts. The lab operates through connections between the Department of Psychology at the University of Cambridge and the Department of Communication Science at VU Amsterdam. The selected candidate will primarily work in Amsterdam while benefiting from this wider international network. About the Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities The Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities at VU Amsterdam consists of nine departments organized across three academic schools: The School of Religion and Theology The School of Social Sciences The School of Humanities The faculty has approximately 900 employees, around 5,000 regular students and approximately 5,000 additional course participants. Its researchers and educators examine major social and cultural questions from interdisciplinary perspectives. This environment can be particularly valuable for a doctoral researcher studying digital influence operations, which involve technology, economics, communication, psychology, politics and culture. About Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam is a major research university located in Amsterdam’s Zuidas district. The university has more than 6,150 employees and approximately 31,000 students. It presents itself as a values-driven institution committed to education, research and social impact. VU Amsterdam emphasizes diversity, inclusion and internationalization. Its academic community includes people from different nationalities, backgrounds, beliefs and worldviews. The university’s Amsterdam location also provides access to a large network of academic institutions, technology companies, public-policy organizations, international businesses and civil-society organizations. Information for Applicants Moving to the Netherlands Applicants who are selected and need to relocate should begin immigration and relocation preparations as early as possible. Immigration requirements depend on nationality and the expected length of stay. Non-European Union nationals who will remain in the Netherlands for more than 90 days generally require a Dutch residence permit and may also require a provisional residence visa, known as an MVV. VU Amsterdam’s International Office provides immigration support for eligible international employees and doctoral candidates. The university explains that it can generally use an accelerated immigration procedure for scientific researchers and highly skilled migrants when the relevant requirements are met. Immigration procedures normally begin after a candidate has been selected and formally onboarded by the supervisor and human-resources team. Residence authorization remains subject to the requirements and decisions of the Dutch immigration authorities. VU Amsterdam also provides relocation information to international doctoral candidates. Limited university-arranged accommodation may be available, but housing is not guaranteed. Candidates relocating to Amsterdam should therefore prepare for the city’s competitive housing market. Applicants can review the university’s official guidance for international employees and PhD candidates and its information for international doctoral candidates . Required Application Documents Candidates should prepare the following documents: An up-to-date curriculum vitae A concise application or motivation letter in English or Dutch, with a maximum length of two pages as stated in the vacancy instructions The motivation letter should directly demonstrate how the applicant meets the requirements of the position. Rather than offering only a general explanation of interest in doctoral study, applicants should connect their experience to the specific research project. A strong letter should address: The applicant’s relevant master’s degree Academic performance and thesis or dissertation research Experience with quantitative research design Knowledge of advanced statistics and time-series analysis Practical experience using Python Practical experience using R Interest in disinformation and digital influence operations Experience working with social-media, behavioural or financial data Any previous experimental research Academic-writing experience Ability to work independently Experience collaborating in interdisciplinary teams Russian or Mandarin proficiency, if applicable Reasons for wanting to join VU Amsterdam and the research project Applicants may also mention relevant publications, conference presentations, open-source code, research assistantships, GitHub projects or reproducible analytical work in their CV when applicable. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the official VU Amsterdam online recruitment system. Email applications will not be accepted. Applicants should: Read the complete official vacancy announcement . Prepare an updated CV. Write a targeted application letter in English or Dutch. Confirm that the letter does not exceed the stated two-page limit. Review the documents for accuracy and consistency. Submit the application through the official VU Amsterdam application portal . Complete the submission before Monday, 14 September 2026 at 23:59. Candidates should apply early enough to resolve any technical problems before the deadline. Selection and Interview Timeline VU Amsterdam expects interviews to take place between 21 and 30 September 2026. Interviews may be conducted in Amsterdam or online. Shortlisted candidates should be prepared to discuss: Their master’s thesis or previous research Their understanding of the online manipulation economy Quantitative methods they have used Their experience with Python and R Their understanding of time-series analysis How they would approach large-scale social-media data Their experience designing experiments Their ability to work independently Their academic and professional objectives Their interest in interdisciplinary research Their availability to begin on 4 January 2027 Applicants invited to interview should review the project description carefully and be ready to propose possible research questions or methodological approaches. Any ideas presented should remain flexible because the final studies will be developed collaboratively with the supervisory team. Important Dates Vacancy publication date: 17 August 2026 Application deadline: Monday, 14 September 2026 at 23:59 Expected interview period: 21–30 September 2026 Preferred starting date: Monday, 4 January 2027 Application Tips for Prospective Candidates Demonstrate both Python and R experience The vacancy identifies experience with both programming languages as essential. Applicants should provide concrete examples of how they have used each language rather than simply listing them under technical skills. Explain your statistical preparation Mention relevant graduate courses and research projects involving advanced statistics. Candidates with time-series analysis experience should make that expertise clearly visible. Connect your thesis to the position Even if the master’s thesis was not specifically about disinformation, applicants can explain how its methods, datasets or theoretical questions prepared them for this project. Show evidence of reproducible research Examples may include documented code, version-controlled projects, preregistered studies, publicly available materials or well-organized analytical workflows. Address the project directly A generic motivation letter is unlikely to demonstrate sufficient preparation. Applicants should explain why the market infrastructure behind digital influence operations is an important research problem and how their skills can contribute to studying it. Demonstrate independence and collaboration The position requires both qualities. Applicants should provide examples showing they can manage complex research tasks independently while communicating effectively with supervisors and interdisciplinary collaborators. Submit before the final day Waiting until the deadline creates unnecessary risk. Applicants should allow time for document conversion, portal errors and any final revisions. Frequently Asked Questions What is the application deadline? The deadline is Monday, 14 September 2026 at 23:59. The vacancy page does not specify a timezone, so candidates should submit well in advance. When will interviews take place? VU Amsterdam expects to conduct interviews between 21 and 30 September 2026. Interviews may be held in Amsterdam or online. When is the preferred starting date? The preferred starting date is Monday, 4 January 2027. What is the monthly salary? The advertised salary starts at €3,204 gross per month and increases to a maximum of €4,051 gross per month in the fourth year for full-time employment. How long does the position last? The total planned duration is four years. The initial contract is for one year and may be extended following a satisfactory evaluation. Are Python and R both required? Yes. The vacancy states that experience with Python and R is essential. Is time-series analysis required? Applicants are expected to have advanced statistical skills, including time-series analysis. Are Russian or Mandarin mandatory? No. Knowledge of Russian and/or Mandarin is an advantage, but it is not listed as a mandatory requirement. Can the position be completed remotely? The position is based primarily at VU Amsterdam. Some supervisory meetings may take place virtually, and interviews may be conducted online, but the vacancy is not advertised as a fully remote doctoral position. Can applications be submitted by email? No. VU Amsterdam states that email applications will not be accepted. Candidates must use the official recruitment portal. Conclusion The fully funded PhD Position in Social Data Science at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam offers an exceptional opportunity to conduct advanced, socially relevant research into the economic infrastructure behind disinformation and digital influence operations. The successful candidate will investigate how fake accounts, artificial engagement and bot networks are produced, marketed, purchased and deployed. By combining social-media information, financial data, experiments, interviews and advanced computational methods, the researcher will help build a deeper understanding of the online manipulation economy and its effects on society. In addition to receiving structured doctoral training and international research exposure, the selected candidate will receive a full-time salary beginning at €3,204 gross per month and increasing to a maximum of €4,051 gross per month in the fourth year. Additional benefits include holiday allowance, a year-end bonus, annual leave and commuting support. Candidates with a relevant master’s degree, advanced statistical knowledge, strong research-design abilities, excellent English academic writing and practical experience in both Python and R should consider applying. Applications must be submitted through the official VU Amsterdam recruitment portal by Monday, 14 September 2026 at 23:59. Because email applications are not accepted and no deadline timezone is specified, prospective candidates should complete their submissions well before the closing time. title: Goldman Sachs Programs and Internships 2026–2027: Global Opportunities for Students and Graduates
summary: Goldman Sachs is inviting students, graduates and early-career professionals to explore a wide range of career opportunities through its global programs, internships, graduate programmes and early-career initiatives for 2026 and 2027. The opportunities span multiple regions, including the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA), Asia-Pacific and India , and cover areas such as investment banking, engineering, asset management, global investment research, operations, risk, compliance, technology, finance, legal, human capital management and wealth management. Goldman Sachs describes its student programmes as opportunities for talented individuals to gain early exposure to the firm, its people and real-world business challenges. The firm says its internships provide hands-on experience, training, networking and opportunities to work alongside experienced professionals. Goldman Sachs Programs and Internships 2026–2027 The official Goldman Sachs careers portal currently features a broad portfolio of student and early-career opportunities. The programmes are not one single scholarship or internship with one universal deadline; instead, applicants can choose programmes according to their academic level, graduation year, location, field of interest and career stage. The current programmes include internships, full-time analyst and associate positions, exploratory programmes and specialised opportunities. Goldman Sachs official programmes page currently lists opportunities across several regions and programme types. 1. Goldman Sachs 2027 Summer Analyst Program – Americas The 2027 Summer Analyst Program in the Americas is designed for undergraduate students who want to experience the day-to-day work of Goldman Sachs. The internship lasts approximately nine to ten weeks during summer 2027. Participants are immersed in the firm s activities and receive training designed to help them succeed. Applicants can potentially explore opportunities in areas including: Asset Management Controllers Corporate Planning and Management Corporate Treasury Engineering Executive Office FICC and Equities Global Investment Research Global Compliance Human Capital Management Internal Audit Investment Banking Legal Office of Regulatory Relations Operations Platform Solutions Risk Tax Wealth Management The programme is generally intended for students currently pursuing a college or university degree, usually in their third or penultimate year of study . For the 2027 cycle, Goldman Sachs states that applications opened on 15 August 2026 . Applicants should check the individual vacancy because availability and application timelines may differ by business and location. 2. Goldman Sachs 2027 Summer Associate Program – Americas The 2027 Summer Associate Program is designed for graduate students seeking exposure to Goldman Sachs and the financial services industry. The programme lasts approximately nine to ten weeks and gives participants an opportunity to work on real responsibilities alongside Goldman Sachs professionals. The programme is intended for candidates pursuing advanced degrees such as: MBA PhD JD MD LLM The summer associate role is generally undertaken during the second or penultimate year of an advanced degree programme . Potential business areas include investment banking, asset management, engineering, global investment research, risk, operations, legal, compliance, wealth management and other functions. 3. Goldman Sachs 2027 Summer Analyst Program – Asia-Pacific Goldman Sachs also offers a 2027 Summer Analyst Internship in Asia-Pacific . The programme is approximately nine to eleven weeks and is designed for students in the penultimate year of their bachelor s or master s degree. Goldman Sachs states that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis , meaning prospective applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as suitable opportunities become available. The programme can provide exposure to areas such as: Asset Management Global Investment Research Investment Banking Engineering Operations Risk FICC and Equities Legal Tax Global Compliance Human Capital Management Internal Audit Corporate Treasury Wealth Management Applicants must check the specific application for available locations and business divisions. 4. Goldman Sachs 2027 Summer Associate Program – Asia-Pacific Graduate students can also consider the 2027 Summer Associate Program in Asia-Pacific . The programme is designed for candidates graduating from an advanced degree programme such as: MBA PhD JD MD LLM For the current cycle, Goldman Sachs indicates that eligible students should generally be graduating between August 2027 and July 2028 . The internship runs for approximately nine to ten weeks and provides exposure to live projects, internal and external clients, professional training and networking opportunities. Goldman Sachs notes that application timelines vary by business, so candidates should monitor the relevant application pages rather than relying on a single universal deadline. 5. Goldman Sachs 2027 Summer Analyst Programme – Europe, Middle East and Africa The EMEA region is particularly relevant to applicants from Africa, including students and graduates seeking international financial services experience. Goldman Sachs EMEA student opportunities include summer internships, work placements, off-cycle internships, engineering opportunities and graduate programmes. Applicants interested in the EMEA Summer Analyst Programme should monitor the official Goldman Sachs careers portal for the relevant business and location. Because Goldman Sachs recruits across different countries and offices, applicants should not assume that every EMEA programme is available in every African or European country. The exact location is provided in the individual application. 6. Goldman Sachs 2027 Summer Associate Programme – EMEA The 2027 EMEA Summer Associate Programme is a graduate-level internship scheduled for Summer 2027 . Goldman Sachs states that applications for the 2027 EMEA Summer Associate programmes opened on 15 August 2026 . The programme is particularly focused on candidates working towards advanced degrees in areas such as: Engineering Computer Science Mathematics Data Science Sciences Other quantitative disciplines The programme lasts approximately 10 weeks and is designed to provide graduate students with hands-on experience and insight into the work they could undertake as full-time Goldman Sachs employees. Participants can receive training, attend orientation and work alongside Goldman Sachs professionals on real responsibilities. 7. Goldman Sachs New Analyst Programmes Goldman Sachs also recruits final-year students through its New Analyst Programmes . These are full-time career opportunities , rather than short-term internships. In the EMEA region, the programme is designed for students graduating with undergraduate or graduate degrees. Successful candidates can develop professional skills, build relationships across the firm and gain experience across different business divisions. The EMEA New Analyst Programme is expected to start in Summer 2027 , while application timelines vary according to the business. The programme can include opportunities in: Asset Management Global Investment Research Investment Banking Engineering Operations Risk Finance Corporate Treasury Legal Tax Compliance Human Capital Management Wealth Management Internal Audit Similar New Analyst opportunities are available in the Americas and Asia-Pacific. For example, the Americas New Analyst Program is intended for students graduating with an undergraduate or graduate degree between December 2026 and July 2027 , with a Summer 2027 start date. In Asia-Pacific, Goldman Sachs states that its New Analyst Program is open to final-year undergraduate and graduate students and can be available across functions including engineering, investment banking and wealth management. 8. Goldman Sachs New Associate Programmes Goldman Sachs also provides full-time opportunities for candidates pursuing careers at the associate level. In the Americas, the New Associate Program is designed for individuals who typically have two to five years of professional experience after undergraduate study , together with an advanced degree such as an MBA, JD, MD or LLM. Eligible candidates for the current Americas cycle are generally graduating between December 2026 and July 2027 . The EMEA New Associate Programme is more specialised in the current listing, with a focus on candidates graduating from advanced degree programmes and, for the listed Engineering programme, candidates with an advanced degree in Engineering or Computer Science and two to five years of experience. 9. Goldman Sachs Work Placement Programme – EMEA Students looking for longer-term professional exposure can consider the Work Placement Programme in EMEA. Unlike a conventional summer internship, this is a year-long programme intended to provide students with substantial industry experience before completing their studies. Goldman Sachs says the programme is suited to students, usually in their penultimate year, who are interested in completing a work placement as part of their degree. Participants can gain experience in areas such as: Wealth Management Tax Controllers Corporate Treasury Human Capital Management Internal Audit Operations FICC and Equities Corporate and Workplace Solutions The programme provides ongoing training and opportunities to undertake real responsibilities alongside Goldman Sachs employees. Goldman Sachs currently states that applications for the Work Placement Programme are open . 10. Goldman Sachs Off-Cycle Internships Goldman Sachs also provides off-cycle internship opportunities, particularly useful for students who may not fit the traditional summer internship calendar. In Asia-Pacific, the firm s Off-Cycle Internship Programme includes opportunities lasting approximately three to twelve months . The programme is designed for: Penultimate-year undergraduate students Final-year undergraduate students Recent graduates Goldman Sachs states that applicants generally need university approval if taking a leave of absence to participate. The firm currently indicates that applications are open for certain functions, including Global Investment Research and Investment Banking , and that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. 11. Goldman Sachs India Opportunities Goldman Sachs also operates dedicated programmes in India. The current opportunities include the 2027 Summer Analyst Program and the New Analyst Program . For the 2027 Summer Analyst Program in India, Goldman Sachs states that applicants should be students graduating from a bachelor s or master s degree programme in 2028 . The internship is expected to last approximately eight to ten weeks and provides exposure to Goldman Sachs businesses and professional environment. The India New Analyst Program is a full-time opportunity for final-year undergraduate and graduate students graduating in 2027 . Applications opened on 1 July , according to Goldman Sachs. 12. Goldman Sachs Degree Apprenticeship Programmes – EMEA Another pathway available through Goldman Sachs is its Degree Apprenticeship Programme in EMEA. This is different from a conventional internship because participants can earn a salary while pursuing an undergraduate degree and developing professional experience. The programmes are available in areas including: FICC and Equities Engineering Operations The apprenticeship pathways are connected with university degree programmes, including programmes at Queen Mary University of London, the University of Warwick and the Walbrook Institute London. Goldman Sachs states that applications for its 2027 apprenticeships will open in Autumn 2026 . The listed locations are London and Birmingham . What Participants Can Expect Goldman Sachs student programmes are designed around its apprenticeship approach, giving students opportunities to learn through practical experience rather than relying exclusively on classroom instruction. Across its internship programmes, participants can expect several forms of professional development. 1. Hands-on professional experience Interns have the opportunity to contribute to real responsibilities and work alongside Goldman Sachs professionals. This can help participants understand how financial services organisations operate and how different business functions contribute to client outcomes. 2. Professional training Goldman Sachs provides training intended to help interns and early-career employees develop the technical and professional skills required for their roles. 3. Networking opportunities Participants can interact with colleagues, professionals and business leaders, allowing them to build relationships that may be valuable throughout their careers. 4. Exposure to multiple business areas Depending on the programme, candidates may gain exposure to investment banking, engineering, asset management, research, operations, compliance, risk, technology, finance and other functions. 5. Potential pathway to full-time employment Goldman Sachs student programmes can serve as an important pathway into longer-term careers. The firm notes that many of its full-time hires are former interns, while its campus hiring programmes are designed to help students transition from university into professional careers. Who Should Consider Applying? These opportunities can be particularly relevant to: Undergraduate students seeking their first major financial-services internship. Students in their penultimate year preparing for a summer internship. Final-year students preparing to enter the workforce. Master s students looking for specialised professional experience. MBA students interested in investment banking, asset management, finance or related fields. PhD students in quantitative or technical disciplines. Students studying engineering, computer science, mathematics, data science and sciences. Recent graduates who meet the requirements of specific off-cycle programmes. Early-career professionals with relevant experience seeking associate-level opportunities. Students interested in technology, financial markets, investment banking, operations, risk, legal, compliance and other professional functions. However, eligibility is programme-specific . Applicants should always check the academic-year, graduation-year, experience and location requirements for the exact position they intend to pursue. Which Fields of Study Are Accepted? One of the notable features of Goldman Sachs programmes is the breadth of academic disciplines represented across its businesses. Depending on the specific programme, opportunities may be available to candidates with backgrounds in: Finance Economics Accounting Business Investment Engineering Computer Science Mathematics Data Science Statistics Sciences Technology Law Human Resources International disciplines Other relevant academic backgrounds Importantly, candidates should not automatically assume that Goldman Sachs opportunities are limited to finance students. Some programmes explicitly recruit students from technical and quantitative disciplines, while other programmes accept students across broader academic backgrounds. What Makes These Opportunities Competitive? Goldman Sachs is a highly competitive global financial institution, and its student recruitment programmes attract significant interest. The firm reported that its 2025 summer internship programme received approximately 365,000 applicants , with a selection rate of less than 1 percent. This means prospective applicants should approach the application process strategically. A strong application should demonstrate: Academic achievement Maintain a strong academic record and clearly present relevant qualifications. Problem-solving ability Highlight situations where you analysed a difficult problem and developed a practical solution. Leadership Demonstrate leadership through employment, university activities, projects, volunteering, entrepreneurship or community initiatives. Communication skills Show that you can explain complex ideas clearly and work effectively with different people. Technical capability For engineering, data, technology and quantitative roles, highlight relevant programming, analytical or technical competencies. Commercial awareness Applicants for financial-services roles should understand major developments affecting markets, companies, investment and the wider economy. Teamwork Provide evidence of successful collaboration with people from different backgrounds. Interest in Goldman Sachs Applicants should understand the specific business or division they are applying to rather than submitting a generic application. Application Deadline There is no single universal deadline for all Goldman Sachs programmes listed on the careers portal. Application dates vary according to the programme, region, business division and recruitment cycle. For the current 2027 opportunities: Americas 2027 Summer Analyst Program: Applications opened 15 August 2026 . EMEA 2027 Summer Associate Programme: Applications opened 15 August 2026 . India 2027 Summer Analyst Program: Applications opened 1 July 2026 . Asia-Pacific 2027 Summer Analyst Program: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis . Asia-Pacific Off-Cycle Internship: Selected opportunities are currently open and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. EMEA Work Placement Programme: Applications are currently open. EMEA 2027 Degree Apprenticeships: Applications are expected to open in Autumn 2026 . Because Goldman Sachs can close applications once sufficient candidates have been identified, applicants should not wait for a final deadline if the relevant application is already open . Countries and Regions Eligible to Apply The Goldman Sachs programmes listed on the careers portal are organised by geographic region rather than being one global application. The major regions include: Americas Europe Middle East Africa Asia-Pacific India For African applicants, EMEA opportunities are particularly important to monitor. Goldman Sachs has historically undertaken recruitment initiatives targeting African university talent, including students from Kenya, Ghana and Nigeria , particularly for engineering opportunities. However, applicants should distinguish between a regional programme and a programme that is available in every country within that region. A candidate living in an EMEA country may still need to meet the location, work authorisation and academic requirements of the particular Goldman Sachs office associated with the vacancy. Race and Diversity Eligibility The programmes should not be interpreted as being restricted to one race or ethnicity unless a particular programme explicitly states otherwise. Goldman Sachs has publicly described efforts to expand access to opportunities for people from diverse backgrounds, including initiatives supporting Black talent, women, LGBT+ candidates, people from lower socio-economic backgrounds and other underrepresented communities. The firm s broader student recruitment approach emphasises diverse skills, interests, experiences and perspectives. Therefore, applicants should check the individual programme description carefully to determine whether a particular diversity-focused initiative has additional eligibility requirements. Important Advice for Applicants Before applying, prospective candidates should: Identify the programme that matches their current academic level. Confirm their expected graduation date. Check whether the programme is available in their country or preferred location. Review the specific business division. Tailor their CV or resume to the role. Highlight relevant technical and transferable skills. Research Goldman Sachs and the business they are applying to. Prepare for competency and technical interviews. Apply as early as possible where applications are rolling. Avoid submitting multiple applications without understanding the requirements of each programme. Use only the official Goldman Sachs careers portal when submitting an application. Goldman Sachs also provides resources for students on understanding its businesses, preparing applications and getting ready for interviews. Visit HERE for more information about the Goldman Sachs Programs and Internships 2026–2027. How to Apply Interested applicants should begin by reviewing the official Goldman Sachs Programs and Internships portal and filtering opportunities according to programme type and region. The official careers page currently contains opportunities across internships, full-time roles, exploratory programmes and other early-career pathways. Applicants should select the specific programme that matches their qualifications and follow the instructions provided in the individual application. APPLY HERE Conclusion The Goldman Sachs Programs and Internships portfolio provides multiple entry points for students, graduates and early-career professionals seeking to build careers in global financial services. From the 2027 Summer Analyst and Summer Associate programmes to New Analyst and New Associate positions, work placements, off-cycle internships and degree apprenticeships , the opportunities cover a wide range of academic backgrounds and professional interests. For African applicants, including candidates from Kenya and other EMEA countries, the EMEA opportunities are particularly worth monitoring, while applicants interested in Asia, India or the Americas can explore programmes specifically designed for those markets. The most important point is that there is no single deadline covering every Goldman Sachs opportunity . Application timelines vary significantly, and several programmes use rolling recruitment. Candidates who meet the eligibility requirements should therefore review the official vacancy and apply as early as possible rather than waiting for a general closing date. With Goldman Sachs emphasis on hands-on experience, training, networking and professional development, these programmes can provide a valuable opportunity for students and graduates seeking to establish themselves in investment banking, technology, finance, research, asset management, operations and other areas of the global financial services industry.
